reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space W, every complete real inner-product normed vector space H, every probability measures mu,nu on W, every feature:W->H, and fixed label:H, assume feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu and under nu. For every real t define the actual positive measure curve(t)=ofReal(1-t) times mu + ofReal(t) times nu, where ofReal(r) is the nonnegative extended-real coefficient max(r,0). For any measure law on W define mean(law)=integral_W feature(w) dlaw(w) in H and risk(law)=norm(mean(law)-label)^2 in R. Define the single scalar potential(w)=2*inner_product(mean(mu)-label,feature(w)). Abbreviate D=integral_W potential(w) dnu(w)-integral_W potential(w) dmu(w). Every integral is the literal Bochner integral over all W under the displayed measure; the potential integrals are real-valued. Then all of the following hold: (1) For every real t in the closed interval [0,1], curve(t) is a probability measure, feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under curve(t), and mean(curve(t))=(1-t) times mean(mu)+t times mean(nu). (2) potential is integrable under mu. (3) potential is integrable under nu. (4) The real function t->risk(curve(t)) has derivative D within the closed interval [0,1] at its endpoint 0, including the actual function value at 0. (5) risk(nu)-risk(mu)-D=norm(mean(nu)-mean(mu))^2. (6) risk(mu)+D<=risk(nu). The vector integrability assumptions are supplied separately under the two endpoint laws; segment integrability and both scalar potential integrability claims are derived. For t in [0,1] the nonnegative coefficients are exactly 1-t and t, and the endpoints are curve(0)=mu and curve(1)=nu, with the corresponding means and risks. The derivative is the right-hand endpoint derivative relative to the specified closed interval: as t approaches 0 through that interval, risk(curve(t))=risk(mu)+t*D+o(abs(t)). It is not a claim of an unrestricted two-sided derivative of this actual measure curve. Outside [0,1] the displayed definition still uses clipped nonnegative coefficients rather than a signed affine combination; probability and affine-mean conclusions are asserted only within [0,1]. The scalar difference D uses the same potential based at mean(mu) and is nu minus mu, never an integral against positive or truncated measure subtraction. Under the supplied integrability D also equals 2*inner_product(mean(mu)-label,mean(nu)-mean(mu)), but the explicit derivative value in the statement is the difference of the actual scalar integrals. The loss is the unhalved squared norm of the feature mean minus label, rather than an integral of pointwise squared residuals. The exact remainder is a nonnegative squared norm; D itself may have either sign. No feature second-moment hypothesis, pointwise continuity, topology on W, or abstract global first-variation assertion on measures is supplied or concluded.
objects: Measurable space W; complete real inner-product normed space H; endpoint probability measures mu,nu; vector-valued feature and fixed label; the actual positive-measure curve on real t; the literal vector mean and unhalved mean-squared loss on measures; the mu-anchored scalar potential; the scalar nu-minus-mu integral difference D; and the closed interval [0,1].
domains: W has only a measurable-space structure. H has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, and CompleteSpace structures, without a finite-dimensionality restriction. mu,nu are probability measures on W. feature:W->H, label:H. curve:R->Measure W uses nonnegative extended-real measure coefficients; mean:Measure W->H is the actual vector Bochner integral; risk:Measure W->R is the displayed squared norm. potential:W->R. The derivative has real parameter and codomain and is relative to Set.Icc(0,1) at 0.
quantifiers: Universally quantify W,H and the stated structures, endpoint probability laws mu,nu, feature, and label. Assume Integrable(feature,mu) and Integrable(feature,nu). All six outer conjuncts then hold for the single fixed collection of let-definitions. The first conjunct quantifies every t:R with 0<=t<=1 and contains three assertions for each t: probability, feature integrability, and affine mean. The derivative is asserted at time 0 within that same fixed interval. Endpoints, feature, and label remain fixed as t varies.
assumptions: Both endpoint measures have mass one. H is explicitly complete and real inner-product normed. The two analytic hypotheses are genuine Bochner integrability of feature under mu and under nu, including almost-everywhere strong measurability and a finite integral of its norm under each respective measure. Segment feature integrability and scalar potential integrability are not assumed. No L2 feature membership, boundedness, differentiability of feature, topology on W, or separate differentiability of the risk curve is imposed.
conclusion: (1) For every real t in the closed interval [0,1], curve(t) is a probability measure, feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under curve(t), and mean(curve(t))=(1-t) times mean(mu)+t times mean(nu). (2) potential is integrable under mu. (3) potential is integrable under nu. (4) The real function t->risk(curve(t)) has derivative D within the closed interval [0,1] at its endpoint 0, including the actual function value at 0. (5) risk(nu)-risk(mu)-D=norm(mean(nu)-mean(mu))^2. (6) risk(mu)+D<=risk(nu). scopes: curve is defined for all real t by actual nonnegative measure operations. On [0,1] its coefficients equal 1-t and t; at 0 it equals mu and at 1 it equals nu, so the derivative uses the genuine endpoint risk value risk(mu). HasDerivWithinAt is the derivative of the actual scalar risk along this measure curve relative to the closed segment, not an unrestricted derivative of its clipped extension outside that segment. Only the first conjunct asserts probability and affine mean along the interval; it does not assert a signed measure interpolation formula outside it. Both scalar integrals use the same potential anchored at mean(mu)-label and paired with feature(w), not feature(w)-label. The subtraction direction is integral under nu minus integral under mu, matching displacement mean(nu)-mean(mu); it is never Measure.sub. The mean is an actual integral, with probability supplied here rather than an extra denominator. The loss is norm(mean-label)^2, not the integral of a squared pointwise loss. Its exact remainder is nonnegative, while D need not be. The conclusion concerns this fixed segment and endpoints; no general differentiable risk on arbitrary parameter laws or global measure-space first-variation notion is asserted. Genuine integrability prevents use of nonintegrable totalization on the asserted segment and potential values.
constant_dependencies: The segment coefficients are exactly ofReal(1-t) and ofReal(t), with no unspecified normalization. The unhalved squared loss gives exact factor 2 in potential and the derived pairing 2*inner_product(mean(mu)-label,mean(nu)-mean(mu)). The remainder has coefficient 1. The derivative value is exactly D, the actual scalar integral difference, depending on the two laws, feature, and label. No unknown bound, smoothness constant, finite-particle parameter, or positivity assumption on D occurs.
